question:
(i) Explain why Coulomb’s law alone is not sufficient to directly find the force on a charge in a system of several charges.
(ii) Two forces of $6\,\text{N}$ and $8\,\text{N}$ act on a charge at right angles to each other. Calculate the magnitude of the resultant force.

options.A:
(i) Coulomb’s law gives each pairwise force; superposition is required to add all individual force vectors
(ii) $F_{\text{net}}=\sqrt{6^2+8^2}=10\,\text{N}$
options.B:
(i) Coulomb’s law directly gives the net force due to all charges without vector addition
(ii) $F_{\text{net}}=14\,\text{N}$
options.C:
(i) Only the largest Coulomb force is considered in a many-charge system
(ii) $F_{\text{net}}=2\,\text{N}$
options.D:
(i) Individual forces are multiplied to obtain the resultant force
(ii) $F_{\text{net}}=48\,\text{N}$
